result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, irrevocably—I would dissolve the illusion of separation between people.

Not through laws or technology or grand declarations, but by rewiring perception itself: so every person could viscerally feel the joy and pain of others as if it were their own. Not as sympathy, but as shared reality. When you harmed another, you’d feel it tear through your own chest. When you lifted someone up, your own spirit would rise with them.

This wouldn’t erase conflict or difference—but it would make cruelty unthinkable, indifference impossible. Wars would collapse under the weight of mutual agony. Injustice would burn its perpetrators as much as its victims. And kindness? It would become as natural as breathing, because helping another would literally sustain you.

The world wouldn’t be "perfect"—but it would finally be human, together.
